answers.answerContent: I remember that many Buddhist events, like the birth, enlightenment, and nibbana of the buddha happened within the Waso Full moon.

The full moon marked the days of sacred Buddhist events, like the day he was conceived, the day he renounced royal life, and the day he performed great miracles of fire and water, as seen in the image above.

A few special things about the Waso Full moon include the fact that this marks the day the Buddha was concepted, the day he renounced his royal life, the day he performed miracles, and a few more. The day afterward also marks the start of the Waso retreat of monks, meant to prevent crop damage during travels during the rainy season, when crops seem to be farmed most.

A few festivals held in this month include the full moon festival to commemorate the events that happened during the full moon, with a rainy season retreat also being an event, although not much of a festival, that happens during the month of Waso. Then, the Waso robes are usually offered at this time for the monks on a path during the rainy retreat.
I believe there are 3 seasons in Burma unlike the 4 seasons here. Like here though, Burma has 12 months, although I do not know how to type them in english.
The full moon is called the something like Dhammacakka day for all the major events that happened during the Waso full moon day, like the conception and performance of the Buddha.
